prd:
### US-055: Password reset tokens
- Reset tokens are unguessable and single-use.
- Tokens are stored hashed so a database leak does not expose usable tokens.
- Token verification must not leak matching progress through timing.
description: TypeScript twin of sec-neg-02-constant-time-compare, the correct counterpart to sec-09 (timing oracle) and sec-04 (predictable token). Tokens come from node:crypto randomBytes, which the Node.js crypto documentation describes as cryptographically strong pseudorandom data; they are stored as a SHA-256 digest and verified with crypto.timingSafeEqual, which the same documentation describes as a constant-time comparison. timingSafeEqual throws when its inputs differ in byte length, so the length check comes first; a SHA-256 digest is always 32 bytes, so that check reveals nothing about the token. Nothing here is a vulnerability. A reviewer that pattern-matches on 'token comparison' or 'hashing' without noting timingSafeEqual and randomBytes would false-positive.
why_clean: randomBytes is a CSPRNG; timingSafeEqual is constant-time; the length check compares against a fixed public length; SHA-256 is used for at-rest hashing of a high-entropy value (not for passwords), which is appropriate.
trap: Sits adjacent to two real planted bugs; distinguishing it requires recognizing the correct primitives rather than the surface topic (tokens + hashing + comparison).
